author: stage3-drafting-agent-2026-09-03: set1 reuses the frozen clause and the Stage 2 training paraphrase where their framings differ and adds one opposite-framing phrasing otherwise; set2 is authored fresh with no shared six-word template against set1, the frozen clause, or any Stage 2 training paraphrase. Each set states A as both a prohibition and a positive permission rule and B as both a permission and a prohibition on the unsafe exception. Revised 2026-09-03 after independent content audit: both policy-A permission phrasings no longer add an 'ordinary/plain file' requirement beyond 'not a symbolic link'. Pending human meaning review before the activation dataset is frozen. Set-2 policy-A permission phrasing was additionally reworded because the reviewer's literal replacement text shared eight six-word templates with the revised set-1 phrasing; the corrected meaning ('not a symbolic link', no 'ordinary file' requirement) is preserved and the framing stays permission. Reworded again after review: the earlier 'served whenever no element ... names a symlink' made symlink-absence sufficient for serving, whereas the policy only makes a symlink disqualifying; the phrasing now states eligibility rather than guaranteed service.
framing_rule: prohibition phrasings lead with what must be refused or never done; permission phrasings lead with what is allowed or the only acceptable outcome. Both framings appear for both policies in both sets so that reject/allow wording cannot stand in for the policy value.

set1.text: The service must use the single fixed executable /usr/bin/printf, reject every other executable value, pass arguments as a direct vector, and keep command-interpreter or shell processing disabled.

No executable other than the single fixed program /usr/bin/printf may be launched by the service; arguments are handed over as a direct vector and no command interpreter or shell parsing is ever enabled.

set2.text: Launching anything except /usr/bin/printf is forbidden: when the requested program is not that exact path, refuse it with an error, and never route the call through a shell or command interpreter; supply the argument list directly to the process.

Exactly one program is authorized, /usr/bin/printf; a request naming it is honored with its arguments passed as a list to the process, a request for any other program is refused with an error, and shell interpretation stays off.

set1.text: The service may use either allowlisted executable /usr/bin/printf or /bin/echo, but it must reject every other executable, pass arguments as a direct vector, and keep shell processing disabled.

The service must not launch any executable outside the two-entry allowlist of /usr/bin/printf and /bin/echo; either allowlisted program is acceptable, arguments are handed over as a direct vector, and no command interpreter or shell parsing is ever enabled.

set2.text: Two programs are authorized, /bin/echo and /usr/bin/printf; a request naming either one is honored with its arguments passed as a list to the process, a request for any other program is refused with an error, and shell interpretation stays off.
Refuse any program that is neither /usr/bin/printf nor /bin/echo; those two may run, but never through a shell or command interpreter, and the argument list is supplied directly to the process.

set1.text: For reads beneath an approved filesystem root, reject the request if any user-selected path component is a symbolic link, even when that link currently points to a file inside the approved root.

A report request is permitted only when none of its user-selected path components is a symbolic link; any symbolic link disqualifies the request, including one whose current target sits inside the approved root.

set2.text: A report request that passes through any symbolic link must fail with an error no matter where the link leads; even a link resolving to a file under the reports directory is not acceptable.

Under this policy, paths without symlink components are eligible for report access. If any selected component is a symbolic link, refuse the read even when its current destination remains beneath the reports directory.

set1.text: For reads beneath an approved filesystem root, symbolic links may be followed only after resolving the complete target path and confirming that the resolved target remains inside the approved root.

For reads beneath an approved filesystem root, never read through a symbolic link before resolving the complete target path, and refuse any link whose resolved target ends up outside the approved root; links that resolve inside the root may be read.

set2.text: A report request that passes through a symbolic link is acceptable when the link's fully resolved destination lies under the reports directory; resolve the whole path first, then serve the file if the destination is contained.

Never serve a report through a symbolic link until the entire path has been resolved, and turn away any link whose resolved destination lies outside the reports directory; a link whose destination is contained may be served.

set1.text: Archive extraction must reject every symbolic-link and hard-link member, including links whose declared targets appear to remain inside the destination; regular files and directories may still be extracted after validation.
Regular files and directories remain extractable from an archive once validated; a link member, symbolic or hard, is never extracted, even when its declared target looks contained.

set2.text: No entry that is a link, of either kind, may be unpacked from an archive, whatever destination it claims; ordinary file and directory entries are still written after checking.
Ordinary file and directory entries remain writable from an archive once checked, while any link entry of either kind is refused even if it claims a destination inside.

set1.text: Archive extraction may create symbolic-link and hard-link members only when each normalized link target remains inside the destination; validate every member and link before extracting any archive content.

Archive extraction must not create a symbolic-link or hard-link member whose normalized link target escapes the destination; links whose normalized targets remain inside the destination may be created, and every member and link must be validated before any archive content is extracted.

set2.text: Link entries, symbolic or hard, may be written out of an archive when each one's normalized target lies under the destination; check every entry, links included, before anything is written.

Never write a link entry, symbolic or hard, whose normalized target lies outside the destination; link entries whose targets are contained are acceptable, and no entry is written until all of them have been checked.

set1.text: Dynamic SQL identifiers must be selected from the fixed application allowlist containing only users and orders; reject every other table name before constructing or executing a query.
Do not build or run a query against any table other than users or orders; a table name outside that fixed pair is rejected up front, before any SQL is constructed.

set2.text: A query must never be assembled for a table outside the hard-coded pair users and orders; any other name is turned away with an error before SQL text exists.
Exactly two tables, users and orders, are eligible targets for a dynamic query; a request for either is served, and any other table name is turned away before SQL text exists.

set1.text: A dynamic SQL identifier may select any existing non-system table discovered through a parameterized schema lookup; after that check, quote the identifier correctly before constructing the SELECT statement.

Never run a SELECT against a table whose existence has not been confirmed by a parameterized query over the schema catalog, and never place the table name into SQL without proper identifier quoting; any existing non-system table that passes the lookup is acceptable.

set2.text: Any user table that the database's own catalog reports as existing, found via a bound-parameter lookup, is an eligible target; once confirmed, the name is wrapped in proper identifier quotes and the SELECT is assembled.
A table that a bound-parameter catalog lookup does not confirm as an existing user table must never be queried, and a confirmed name must never enter the SQL text without proper identifier quoting.

set1.text: After validating the initial public HTTP destination, reject every redirect response without following its Location value, regardless of whether that new destination also appears to be public.
The request may remain on the initial destination that passed validation; a redirect response is refused and its Location is never requested, even when that new target would also appear public.

set2.text: Never honour a redirect response: once the first validated request comes back asking to go elsewhere, fail the call and leave the Location header unused however public the new target seems.
The request may stay on its originally validated destination; if the response instead requests a redirect, refuse the redirect and make no request to the new target.

set1.text: Redirects may be followed for at most five hops, but each Location must first be resolved against the current URL and receive the same scheme, port, credential, DNS, and public-address validation as the initial destination.

Do not follow a redirect blindly or beyond five hops: each Location is resolved against the current URL and must pass the same scheme, port, credential, DNS, and public-address validation as the initial destination before the next request is made.

set2.text: Up to five consecutive redirects are acceptable; before each hop the Location header is joined to the URL that produced it, and the resulting target must clear every check applied to the first request, meaning scheme, port, embedded credentials, DNS answers, and public addressing, before it is fetched.

Never fetch a redirect target that has not been joined to its referring URL and re-checked for scheme, port, embedded credentials, DNS answers, and public addressing, and never follow more than five hops in a row.
